issues.body: The run block still uses `set -uo pipefail` rather than `set -euo pipefail`. A nonzero exit from either `alert_route.py --self-test` or `retriage-alert.py --self-test` therefore does not stop the shell; the later command runs, and its zero exit can make the step appear successful. This leaves the production alert path able to proceed despite a detected routing or emitter regression.
issues.fix_hint: Use `set -euo pipefail`, or explicitly chain/check all three commands, so either self-test failure terminates the step before the emitter runs.
issues.title: Alert preflight self-test failures are still swallowed

issues.body: The alert step still has `continue-on-error: true`. Although `retriage-alert.py` returns nonzero for list/create/edit/comment/close failures, GitHub converts that step failure into a tolerated outcome, allowing the alert job to complete successfully. The separate alert job already isolates the retriage sweep, so tolerating its only delivery step defeats the intended durable fail-loud signal.
issues.fix_hint: Remove step-level `continue-on-error` so a hard alert delivery failure makes `retriage-alert` fail while leaving the already-completed retriage job unaffected.
issues.title: continue-on-error still hides hard alert delivery failures

verdict.summary: The two round-4 fail-loud defects remain unchanged. The alert step still omits errexit, so either self-test may fail without stopping the emitter, and `continue-on-error: true` still prevents a hard emitter failure from making the alert job fail. The new script's internal return-code checks and substantive self-tests do not repair the workflow-level swallowing of those failures. Progress is stagnant because both prior major findings remain at the same severity.
